headline: Cheniere swings to profit, raises full-year guidance again
summary_short: Cheniere's Q2 2026 revenue slipped 2.3% q/q but rose 23.5% y/y to $5,732M as net income swung to $3,068M from a $3,502M derivative-driven loss in Q1, and the company again raised its full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance to $7.90B-$8.40B and Distributable Cash Flow guidance to $5.30B-$5.80B.
summary_long: Revenue grew 23.5% y/y to $5,732M on higher LNG volumes (184 cargoes, +19% y/y) and stronger delivered margins. Net income of $3,068M reversed Q1's derivative-driven $3,502M loss, mainly on favorable IPM fair-value swings plus higher delivered margins. Adjusted EBITDA rose 27.4% y/y to $1,804M. Cheniere raised full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance to $7.90B-$8.40B (from $7.25B-$7.75B), Distributable Cash Flow guidance to $5.30B-$5.80B (from $4.75B-$5.25B), and tightened 2026 LNG production guidance upward to 53-54 mtpa. Cash fell to $1,099M after $884M deployed on buybacks, dividends and equity-funded growth capex; long-term debt rose to $22,632M after a $1.75B Cheniere Partners senior notes issuance, partly used to redeem $1.5B of SPL notes.

drivers.explanation: Company attributes the y/y increase to higher LNG volumes delivered (184 cargoes vs 154, +19% y/y; 672 vs 550 TBtu, +22% y/y) and higher margins per MMBtu.

Swing to profit driven by roughly $1.4B of favorable derivative fair-value changes on long-term IPM agreements plus higher delivered margins from higher volumes, partly offset by higher non-controlling-interest income.
Follows the net income swing, aided by a lower diluted share count (209.5M vs 222.3M y/y) from continued buybacks.
Tracks the same higher-volume, higher-margin drivers the release cites for net income and Adjusted EBITDA.
Company attributes the $388M y/y increase to higher total margins on LNG delivered, from both higher volumes and higher margins per MMBtu delivered.
Declined after $884M deployed under the capital allocation plan this quarter: approximately $550M of buybacks, $116M of dividends, and equity-funded growth capex.
Cheniere Partners issued $1.75B of senior notes in June 2026, using proceeds partly to redeem $1.5B of SPL's 5.00% notes due 2027 and fund SPL Expansion Project costs.
Rebounded q/q as Q2's $3,068M net income restored equity after Q1's large derivative-driven loss, though y/y equity is still down on cumulative treasury-stock buybacks.
Falls y/y and q/q as the company continues repurchasing shares under its capital allocation plan (2.2 million shares repurchased in Q2 alone).
CEO Jack Fusco called it 'another outstanding quarter,' citing substantial completion of Midscale Train 6 and progress toward FID on Phase 1 of the SPL Expansion Project alongside the guidance raise.
